_note: Infrastructure only. No recordings, transcripts, quotes or speakers are included or generated. Every fact carries a source and url of a page that was fetched on the checked date. Speaker counts vary by source; where a field could not be verified from a fetched page it is omitted or marked 'not assessed'.

_recording_schema.place_slug: place slug from the pack places.json or web/data/diorama/<slug>
_recording_schema.speaker_credit: name or pseudonym the speaker chose, with their stated role; required
_recording_schema.consent_ref: id of the signed consent record held by the partner organisation; required
_recording_schema.licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 or CC BY-NC 4.0 as chosen by the speaker; required
_recording_schema.audio_url: URL of the audio file, served only after consent is recorded
_recording_schema.transcript: original-language transcript, as agreed with the speaker
_recording_schema.translation_en: English translation, as agreed with the speaker

languages.name: Torwali
languages.where_spoken: Bahrain (Sinkaen) and Chail valleys of Swat Kohistan, upper Swat Valley; Madyan separates the two valleys
languages.speakers_estimate: About 130,000 native speakers (2020, Ethnologue as cited on Wikipedia); about 140,000 (2021, cited on Wikipedia)
languages.status: Vulnerable (Catalogue of Endangered Languages, as cited on Wikipedia); revitalisation efforts since 2004

languages.name: Gawri (Kalami)
languages.where_spoken: Kalam tahsil, Swat, and Swat Kohistan / Dir Kohistan
languages.status: Classified as endangered; Pashto, Urdu and other dominant languages are displacing it, especially among urban migrants and younger generations

languages.name: Pashto
languages.where_spoken: Regional language of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and northern Balochistan (Wikipedia, Pashto)
languages.speakers_estimate: About 51 million first-language speakers (2017-2023) and 4.9 million second-language (2022), Ethnologue as cited on Wikipedia

languages.name: Gujari (Gojri)
languages.where_spoken: Azad Kashmir (all ten districts), Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (Hazara, Swat, Dir, Chitral, Kaghan, Kohistan), Gilgit-Baltistan, and plains of Punjab (Wikipedia, Gujari). Wider-region language, not specific to Swat.
languages.speakers_estimate: About 800,000 in Azad Kashmir (2001, Baart and Baart-Bremer, cited on Wikipedia); about 223,505 Gujjar speakers in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (an estimate, not from a census, per Wikipedia)
languages.status: No formal rating in the article; many Gujjars in the plains have stopped speaking Gujari, and a government-backed revival programme exists

languages.name: Ushojo (Ushoji)
languages.where_spoken: Districts of Kohistan and Swat, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (Wikipedia, Ushoji language)
languages.speakers_estimate: About 2,000 native speakers (cited 1992; Ethnologue 2015 edition, as cited on Wikipedia)
languages.status: May be severely endangered because of Pashto dominance, especially in Swat (Wikipedia; assigning body not named)
